title: Recirculation: Giving Transformers a Persistent State
summary: Deep-to-shallow feedback gives a feedforward Transformer a lightweight persistent state by recirculating representations from deeper layers back into shallower computation. This approach effectively turns the model into a dynamical system without retraining its core weights, enabling information to persist and evolve across computation cycles while preserving the underlying pretrained model.
category: Recirculation + Persistent State + Transformers + Deep-to-Shallow Feedback + Dynamical Systems + LLM Architecture + Efficient AI

title: The Reliability Gap: Why Agent Success Is Not Agent Reliability
summary: ThinkingBox distinguishes between an agent finding one successful trajectory and reliably executing the correct state transition across repeated attempts. The framework evaluates whether agents can reproduce intended behavior consistently rather than treating isolated task success as sufficient evidence of reliability, highlighting repeatability, state correctness, and behavioral consistency as critical dimensions of production agent systems.
category: Agent Reliability + Agent Evaluation + State Transitions + Repeatability + ThinkingBox + Production Agents + Robust Agentic AI

title: Pandora: Routing Intelligence by Value
summary: Pandora explores how AI systems can learn when additional computation is worth its cost. Instead of applying the same reasoning depth to every problem, value-aware routing seeks to allocate deeper computation selectively based on expected benefit. This reframes inference-time scaling as a routing problem that connects reasoning quality, computational cost, task difficulty, and economic value.
category: Inference-Time Scaling + Value-Aware Routing + Adaptive Computation + Reasoning Systems + AI Economics + Compute Allocation + Intelligent Routing

title: The Strategy Gap in AI Post-Training
summary: This work highlights the distinction between optimizing an existing strategy and recognizing when the strategy itself should change. Agents can become increasingly effective at improving individual steps within a predefined path while remaining unable to reconsider the broader approach. The resulting strategy gap suggests that post-training must address not only local execution quality but also higher-level strategic adaptation and path re-evaluation.
category: AI Post-Training + Agent Strategy + Strategic Reasoning + Agent Optimization + Planning + Adaptive Agents + Agentic AI

title: Agentic AI Breaks LLM Serving
summary: Agentic workloads challenge conventional LLM-serving architectures because agents generate irregular, stateful, multi-step workloads rather than predictable streams of independent requests. This work argues that AI infrastructure must evolve beyond optimizing token throughput toward serving complete agent execution workloads, introducing new requirements around scheduling, orchestration, state management, tool use, latency, and resource allocation.
category: Agentic AI + LLM Serving + AI Infrastructure + Workload Serving + Inference Systems + Scheduling + Agent Execution

title: From Glucose Signals to Metabolic Intelligence
summary: GlucoFM explores how foundation-model approaches can transform continuous glucose measurements into representations of metabolic state across multiple timescales. Rather than treating glucose values as isolated measurements, the approach learns temporal patterns that capture broader metabolic dynamics, illustrating how foundation models can move physiological AI from signal prediction toward richer representations of biological state.
category: Foundation Models + Glucose Modeling + Metabolic Intelligence + Time-Series AI + Health AI + Representation Learning + Physiological Signals

title: The Re-Query Tax: What Context Compression Hides in Agent Performance
summary: This work examines how context compression can reduce visible context size without necessarily improving overall agent efficiency. When important information is lost, agents may compensate through additional retrieval, repeated questioning, or interaction loops. The resulting re-query tax can increase interaction cost even when task-completion rates remain relatively stable, revealing why token-level efficiency metrics alone can hide important dimensions of agent performance.
category: Context Compression + Agent Performance + Re-Query Cost + Interaction Efficiency + Long Context + Agentic AI + Inference Economics

title: The Capability Gap in Agent Evaluation
summary: This work examines the difference between an agent possessing a capability and that capability actually contributing to runtime performance. By focusing on what agent skills truly add during execution rather than assuming that available capabilities automatically improve outcomes, the research exposes a gap between nominal capability and realized capability and provides a stronger lens for evaluating practical agent performance.
category: Agent Evaluation + Agent Skills + Runtime Capability + Capability Measurement + Agentic Systems + Benchmarking + Execution Analysis

title: Jagged Judges: The Hidden Fragility of AI Judgment
summary: Jagged Judges investigates the stability of AI judgment under repetition, challenge, and adaptive pressure. Rather than treating an evaluator's decision as a single reliable measurement, the work examines whether AI judgments remain consistent when decisions are revisited or evaluation conditions change, exposing epistemic instability as an important dimension of AI evaluation and trustworthy agent assessment.
category: AI Evaluation + LLM Judges + Epistemic Stability + Judge Reliability + Adaptive Evaluation + Agent Evaluation + Trustworthy AI
